A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, 13 figures, two tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Swiss rolls, galaxy classification, vector fields, and molecular properties, including results in Figures 3–9, Table 1, and Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes.

M1.justification: The architectures, prediction heads, and training losses in the experiments and Appendices B–E are retained. Expanded evidential-regression explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Swiss rolls, Galaxy Zoo DESI/SDSS images under PSF blurring, spiral and sinusoidal vector fields, and QM9s scalar properties and spectra. No evaluated domain or scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same MLP versus invariant/equivariant comparisons, CNN and group-convolution comparisons, and GIN versus E(3)-invariant molecular comparisons remain. No comparator membership changes within these experiments.

E3.justification: Evaluation settings are retained, including 100-bin ECE, the vector-field experiment's 2,000 samples and 10–100 training epochs, and the appendix preprocessing, regularization choices, and model sizes. Figure 3's revised axis label clarifies the existing symmetry proportion.

E4.justification: The symmetry-mismatch sweeps, PSF/group-order analyses, rotation-angle losses, molecular uncertainty diagnostics, and Appendix E's regularizer-sensitivity observation are unchanged. No additional ablation or robustness test is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, or empirical confidence intervals. Predictive-uncertainty plots and Appendix C's Hoeffding-bound discussion are retained; the expanded uncertainty definitions do not change statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1's values and the empirical plots match, including Appendix F. For example, both report LUMO MAEs of 0.4404 for GIN and 0.6710 for the E(3)-invariant model, and spectral aleatoric bleed of approximately 17.613. No result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: v4 adds an SO(n) fundamental-domain example and a formal Bayes-predictor definition, and permits manifolds with boundary in Assumption 2. The main bounds and proofs remain; the integration formula added to Section 3.4 already appeared in Appendix A. The new example's intersection claim is overbroad for n ≥ 3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusions retain the same calibration bounds, generalized regression metric, aleatoric-bleed contribution, and claims about symmetry mismatch. Introductory rewording does not substantively strengthen or narrow these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion of coverage-based alternatives to GENCE and explains choosing evidential regression over mutual-information decompositions. Section 6.1 adds convergence caveats and discussion of estimating aleatoric uncertainty from samples or domain knowledge. Existing experimental interpretations and principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 10 changes the stated code location from EdwardBerman/EquivariantUQBounds to EdwardBerman/EquiUQ. Implementation and data-processing details in the appendices are otherwise retained. The PDFs do not establish whether repository contents changed.

R1.justification: v4 adds Chau et al. (2025), Rezende and Mohamed (2015), Bengs et al. (2022), and Meinert et al. (2023), and expands discussion of alternative uncertainty frameworks. The central positioning relative to Wang et al. remains unchanged; bibliographic publication updates are not new works.

P1.justification: v4 edits prose and cross-references, expands uncertainty background, adds Section 6.1 Preliminaries, and exchanges the order of Sections 5.4 and 5.5. These are localized explanatory and organizational revisions within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with labeled axes and an expanded caption; Figure 3 replaces its verbal horizontal-axis label with an explicit fraction. Figure 1 is repositioned, and publication headers are added. The remaining scientific displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 improves accessibility through clearer uncertainty explanations, corrected cross-references, and figure labels, while retaining v1's empirical evidence. However, new Example 1 claims distinct SO(n) rotations produce domains intersecting only at zero. For n ≥ 3, distinct rotations fixing the first axis leave the proposed domain unchanged, contradicting this claim and its asserted satisfaction of Assumption 2. The explanatory gains coexist with a new mathematical inaccuracy, making the net quality change unclear.
